questions.ask: Does this service own its database schema, with goose migrations in db/migrations?
questions.why: Yes installs .squawk.toml, the settings of the migration linter the quality gate runs on every new migration. No suits a service that reads a schema another repo owns. Either way the tests run against a real PostgreSQL with db/roles.sql applied, the gate's migration checks say 'nothing to check' while db/migrations does not exist, and the migration guard stays silent until it does.
questions.detect: db/migrations exists or go.mod requires github.com/pressly/goose/v3: yes; the schema lives in another repository: no

questions.ask: Run agent-config-kit's Go quality gate on every pull request (.github/workflows/quality-gate.yml)?
questions.why: Installs a small caller of the kit's be-go-quality-gate workflow, pinned to one commit: gates.list again, the coverage floor, a PostgreSQL 18 database built from the migrations, squawk, govulncheck, secret scans and the build, with a read-only token and no secrets. It needs GitHub Actions; an existing quality-gate.yml is kept either way.
questions.detect: the repo is on GitHub (a github.com remote or a .github/ folder); .github/workflows/quality-gate.yml already exists

questions.ask: Review each pull request with DeepSeek, a low-cost paid AI model (.github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml)?
questions.why: Installs a caller of agent-config-kit's reusable DeepSeek review, with notes about this stack: one comment per pull request from a branch of this repository, updated when the repository's owner, a member or a collaborator comments /ask-deepseek. It reads the diff over the GitHub API and runs no pull-request code. It needs the repository secret DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and costs about ten US cents a review at most, usually a cent or two (the diff and the answer are capped); without the secret it passes and sends nothing.
questions.detect: .github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml already exists, or the user has asked for an AI review in CI

questions.ask: Add pull-request templates for work pull requests and dev → prod promotions (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/)?
questions.why: They list only what the gate cannot decide: the error codes an operation declares, the migration and query checks a person reads, and the migration and deploy steps of a promotion. They assume dev and prod branches.
questions.detect: branches dev and prod exist (git branch --list dev prod); .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/ already has files

questions.ask: Does an agent need to read a self-hosted analytics API from this repo?
questions.why: Adds .claude/ANALYTICS.example.md, a template to fill in for that read API. An unfilled template is worse than none, because an agent will try to use it.
questions.detect: the code or .env.*.example names an analytics client, or .claude/ANALYTICS.md exists

questions.ask: Do you open several repositories as one Serena workspace?
questions.why: Adds .claude/SERENA-WORKSPACE.example.md, which explains how to scope Serena's searches across repos. With a single repo the default needs no documentation.
questions.detect: .mcp.json runs Serena and a .serena/project.yml above this repo lists several folders, or AGENT_WORKSPACE_ROOT is set

questions.ask: Seal request and response bodies between this service and its callers (the payload contract: encrypted envelopes, a registry generated from the spec, checked before merge)?
questions.why: Yes installs the payload contract in Go, standard library only: internal/payload (AES-256-GCM envelopes bound to method, route and status; P-256 key agreement with browsers and apps; key rings for server callers; the strict/off switch; the registry generated from api/openapi.json) with tests at 100% that read the shared vectors, the net/http middleware in internal/httpapi, the five ENVELOPE_* codes in internal/apperr, the payload variables in internal/config, payload.config.json, the key script, the contract document and its rules. Four steps stay yours: add the five codes to Registered() and to Problem.code in api/openapi.yaml; add GET /api/payload/handshake when browsers or apps call the service, and exempt it and the health probe as none in payload.config.json; wire the middleware into NewRouter and main; regenerate the server and the registry. The gates stay red until the spec lists the codes, on purpose: a half-adopted contract never passes. Answer no when bodies need no sealing beyond TLS.
questions.detect: payload.config.json or internal/payload/ already exists, or the browsers, apps or services that call this one seal their bodies
